payload.text: The Brennecke Institute originated thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery research, using the dopant to reduce electrolyte crossover. An independent Halvorsen-Pike Laboratories audit superseded the initial 12,000-cycle claim, finding a corrected cycle life of 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold; the earlier figure was retracted because of an un-normalized depth-of-discharge. The prototype’s gravimetric energy density was 148 Wh/kg, and its projected stack-level cost was $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. The chemistry has an operating-temperature floor of 4 °C, below which the dopant precipitates and cycling must stop.
